lines: Evening, Sister. The lamps are lit.
Bless you, Tomas. Go easy on the oil. It's the last cask.
Oi, lamp-man! Sell you a flint? Best in the valley.
Forty years I've lit these lamps without your flints.
And look how well that's gone.
Everything's wet. Even the bread sweats.
The bread's always sweated. You bake it.
Closer to the fire, little one. You're shivering.
The lady in the water used to hum like the kettle does.
Every day I pray, Sister. Still the candle burns low.
Then pray tomorrow, Agnes. That's all any of us can do.
Up off those stones, Agnes. Your knees will set like wax.
The saint can't hear me standing up.
Want to swing the axe, runt?
Why do you light them when it's already dark?
Because it's dark, child. That's when they're for.
No carts again today. The Gatehouse still shut?
The Tollwarden lets nothing through that hasn't paid.
They say the Tollwarden fell. Old Anselm.
He kept a count of every one he sent down. Did you know that?
I didn't. I wish I didn't.
Those carts from the Works. The robes on them...
We ate by that smoke, Bede. For years.
The iron box by the fire groaned last night!
That's the lift, love. Someone's woken it.
She's stopped singing. I can't hear her at all now.
The bell's quiet up there. First time in my life.
The Chandler rang it every dusk for forty years.
Who's the hooded man on the board?
Smell that? Salt. The wind's off the sea tonight.
That's the stew, love. I put the fish in.
Then the stew smells like home.
Up and walk a bit, Jost. You'll grow into that log.
The log and I have an understanding.
Do you think we'd have come, if we'd known?
You'd have come. I'd have come to fetch you.
Pass me more of that kindling.
It's across the fire. My arms are across the fire from it.
Forty years married to a pair of feet.
Lamp's lit for the camp, Ulla. So you can find your way back.
I only go as far as the well, Tomas.
Still wearing that shell, old man?
Only one of us has seen the sea, lamp-man.
And only one of us can find the privy in the dark.
Leave me a bucket, Hedda. The stew's gone thick.
Take two. And don't tell Bede, he'll want stew.
Heard the new one's been down the Mire.
And came back? Then they're luckier than my brother.
They say the Gatehouse is open. We could go on up.
With those knees? We'd get there for the funeral. Ours.
The bell's stopped. Listen, Ulla. Just the fire.
I'd forgotten what the fire sounded like.
Aldith. Brother Col. The weaver's girl...
...and the one with the limp. I never got his name.
Easy, little flame. The wind's only passing.
Sixty-one. Sixty-two... no. Sixty-one. One went out.
Come on, you slippery old bishop. Bite.
Hmm-hm-hmm... no. Not that song. Not in here.
One for the catch. One for my mother. One for whatever's under the bath.
Forty stone received, forty stone rendered. Balanced.
Was that the lift? No. No, just the pipes.
Nearly out of ink. I could write in tallow, I suppose. There's enough.
I saved you the heel of the loaf, Hobb.
The heel! The Prior eats the middle, does he?
The Prior doesn't eat any more.
It's wax, Hobb. It'll be back by dark.
Then you'll have missed it twice.
Did you hear the bell last night? It rang thirteen.
It rings what it likes now. Don't count, lad.
Forty years I rang her. I never heard her stop.
Does it sound strange? The quiet?
It sounds like I can sleep.
